title: What this means for energy traders — Friday, November 20, 2026

sections.overall: No trend is CONFIRMED in today's digest, so this note leans on individual stories rather than established company momentum. The common thread is supply security: Middle East chokepoint risk, Russian refinery strikes and UK storage worries all appear alongside a steady flow of LNG contracting and project approvals. Everything here comes from headlines and summaries only; no articles were opened, and the material is unverified.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: The IEA's message, per the FT headline, is that markets can manage without the Strait of Hormuz but only with time and investment. EIA data in the digest show chokepoint oil flows up 19% in the third quarter. Rigzone reports US commercial crude stocks of 417.797 million barrels as of November 13, up over 3 million barrels on the week, and says the war premium on US sour crude has vanished. Headlines on the US blockade and Iranian cargo transfers keep the geopolitical thread alive. Deal flow continues: Chevron is reported close to buying Beacon Offshore Energy and EnQuest is exiting the UK North Sea. In general, rising stocks alongside supply-risk headlines pull in opposite directions, and which dominates is unclear.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: US storage ended the injection season at 3,810 Bcf, almost 2% above the five-year average, per the EIA. The digest also notes an EIA outlook projecting lower Henry Hub prices in 2026 and 2027. Contracting remains active: Venture Global and China Gas upsized to 1.0 MTPA, Woodside signed with Trafigura, and FERC approved Cheniere's Sabine Pass Stage 5. US LNG exports reached 40 cargoes in the week ending November 18, while spot LNG shipping rates fell for a second week. In the UK, SSE's threat to close a storage site raises security-of-supply questions. Long-dated contracts and approvals are usually read as supportive of future demand for US gas, though timing is uncertain.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: Diesel is the pressure point. UK inflation reached 3.6% on record fuel prices, heating oil costs are weighing on households, and Russia is importing record petrol volumes after Ukrainian refinery strikes. Against that, US diesel dropped below $6 a gallon, a two-month low. Refinery outages and strong diesel cracks are typically associated with firm margins, but the retreat in US diesel shows the picture is mixed.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: The EU and UK have finished negotiations to link their emissions trading systems, though the timetable remains uncertain; Carbon Pulse said that uncertainty contributed to EUAs' largest weekly drop since February. Other regulatory items: the EU's CBAM crediting method with a 10% cap on Article 6 credits, draft CBAM declaration rules, and CRCF carbon farming methodologies due in the Official Journal on November 27. At COP31, the cover decision draft keeps carbon removal while dropping fossil fuel references. The Government of Canada's durable removal procurement, which includes Remova Carbon Systems, adds to buyer-side activity.
